text: Okay, let's talk about nourishing the body. Like, what the heck does that actually mean? So the body runs on nutrients. Nutrients meaning micro nutrients like vitamins and minerals and macro nutrients like carb, scats, and protein. Our body needs vitamin A for our eyes, zinc for our skin, fats for every cell membrane of our body. We need nutrients in order for our bodies to work properly. But here's the catch. The body is incapable of making nutrients. The body literally does not know how to make a mineral or a vitamin. So we must get these nutrients from an outside source, aka food, and put them into the body. So we're giving it the tools that it needs to survive, thrive, and be nourished. It's basically like gas for a car. You need gas in your car in order for it to work properly and run. But cars don't make gas on their own. To go to the gas station, get filled up, and then they can run properly. Humans are the same way, but with nutrients. So what are the foods that contain the most amount of nutrients where we can get the biggest bang for our buck? Whole nutrient dense foods. AKA foods that would be available to us if we were living on a farm 100 years ago. veggies, high-quality protein, bone broth, eggs, fruit, nuts and seeds.
